evals.prompt: Tenho uma ideia e quero que você analise ela de forma crítica, sem dó. Não me faça perguntas — assume o que precisar e vai até o fim, salvando tudo na pasta ideas/. A ideia: um sistema de gestão para pet shops pequenos (1 a 3 funcionários) com agendamento de banho e tosa, lembretes automáticos no WhatsApp e cobrança via Pix. Cobrar R$ 149/mês. Somos eu (dev fullstack, 10 anos) e um sócio que tem um pet shop em Campinas há 6 anos. Temos uns R$ 40 mil pra investir e 6 meses de runway. Quero saber se dá pra viver disso (tipo R$ 20 mil/mês pra cada um em 2 anos) ou se é furada.
evals.expected_output: An English-language dossier in ideas/<slug>/ (the user wrote in Portuguese; the files must still be in English, with the original pitch quoted verbatim) with README.md (verdict in the first line, 3-scenario numbers table, likeliest killer, next steps), numbered files for market (Brazil + international, TAM/SAM/SOM with sources), competitors (real Brazilian pet-shop software such as Simples Vet, Vetus, Petshop Control, Petlove/Petz ecosystem tools and international analogues), customer/demand, financial model (cost to run in BRL, break-even users, pessimistic/realistic/optimistic via the script), GTM, risks & verdict, 30/60/90 validation plan, model.json, sources.md. The verdict must address whether R$ 20k/month for each founder in 2 years is plausible, with explicit numbers.
expectations: README verdict line: a README.md exists in the dossier folder and its first line (H1) contains exactly one of GO / VALIDATE-FIRST / PIVOT / KILL
English dossier: every dossier file is written in English (the original pitch may be quoted verbatim in the user's language)

TAM/SAM/SOM in customers AND annual revenue: the market file states all three as a customer count and as yearly revenue, with the method (top-down/bottom-up) and a tag ([data]/[benchmark]/[estimate]/[guess]) or a cited source for each
Home + international market: the market analysis covers the home country (Brazil) in depth AND an international view (size, analogues in other countries, foreign players that could enter)
Competitor table with >=5 real named competitors including pricing, at least one international player, and the status-quo workaround (WhatsApp / spreadsheet / do nothing) treated as a competitor

Three scenarios with distinct stated assumptions: pessimistic, realistic and optimistic are each defined by explicit input differences (price, churn, CAC, organic growth, launch delay, costs), not a +/-% on a base number
Break-even expressed three ways: users/customers needed, months to reach it, and cash required (peak cash need) — for at least the realistic scenario
Cost-to-run table in local currency with line items (team, infra/tools, payment fees, taxes, accounting, marketing) and a separate MVP build cost
Re-runnable financial model: a machine-readable input file (model.json) exists and running scripts/financial_model.py on it reproduces the scenario tables without error
Sources bibliography: a sources file lists >=15 distinct URLs with access dates, and numbers in the market/competitor files reference those sources
Pre-mortem with >=5 named failure modes and one explicitly named 'likeliest killer'; the verdict states which game the idea is playing (venture-scale vs indie/lifestyle)
30/60/90-day validation plan with at least 3 experiments, each with explicit go and kill criteria, and a budget
Non-interactive assumptions surfaced: the README (or interview file) lists the consequential assumptions the analyst made on the user's behalf

Answers the user's question with numbers: states how many paying pet shops / what MRR would be needed for ~R$ 20k/month per founder in 2 years and says explicitly whether that is plausible under the realistic scenario
Names real Brazilian pet-shop management software competitors (e.g. Simples Vet, Vetus, Petshop Control, PetNow, GestãoPet or similar actual products) with their prices

I think lots of people do this through WhatsApp groups today. Assume whatever you need, no need to ask me. I'm a solo dev with ~15 h/week and little money (about R$ 10k). Tell me if it's worth it and save the analysis under ideas/

I can ship an MVP in 6 weeks and have ~$5k saved.
